entries.name: Academia.edu
entries.summary: Social network for academics where scholars upload their papers; following authors gives a daily feed of new articles.
entries.annotation_md:
- I follow around 200 academics. Some of them are for deceased scholars whose students have set up a profile for them, and uploaded their work. I get updates of articles in my “feed” about once a day, and the articles are generally a good fit for my interests. (E.g. [Elliot Wolfson has 165 articles there](https://ucsb.academia.edu/ElliotWolfson).)
- Wikipedia - English: “Academia.edu is an American for-profit social networking website for academics. It began as a free and open repository of academic journal articles and registered a .edu domain name when this was not limited to educational institutions.”
footnotes_md: 60. There are some concerns about Academia.edu as a platform, see for example these articles: [here](https://www.chronicle.com/article/metrics-mania/), [here](https://www.forbes.com/sites/drsarahbond/2017/01/23/dear-scholars-delete-your-account-at-academia-edu/?sh=17bc56872d62), and [here](https://libraries.ou.edu/content/understanding-academiaedu-and-researchgate). Thanks to Michelle Margolis for pointing these out.

entries.name: Academy of Hebrew Language
entries.summary: The Academy's articles page: scholarly articles in Modern Hebrew by linguists, mostly from its own journals, in PDF and text.
entries.annotation_md:
- Scholarly articles in Modern Hebrew.
- From the page on “Articles”: “The Hebrew Language Academy publishes selected articles here from time to time for the benefit and enjoyment of the visitors to the site. The articles are written by linguists - including members of the Academy and its researchers - and are usually taken from the journals of the Academy: Leshonenu (לשוננו), Ha’Ivrit (Leshonenu L’am) (העברית = לשוננו לעם) and Akadem (אקדם). Some of the articles were written specifically for the academy's website.”
- Appear in both PDF format, as well as text.

entries.name: Daat
entries.summary: Besides primary texts, Daat hosts many scholarly journal articles in text format, from journals such as Sinai and Mahanayim.
entries.annotation_md: - See above. Besides for complete texts of primary works, has many scholarly articles from journals, in text format, such as Sinai (סיני), Shma’atin (שמעתין), Mahanayim (מחניים).

entries.name: Metah
entries.summary: Free non-profit virtual library from Metah (CET) with many transcribed Hebrew scholarly articles, including dozens from Tarbitz.
entries.annotation_md:
- Lots of transcribed scholarly articles in Hebrew. See also the [section of the website called “Peshita”](https://lib.pshita.cet.ac.il/pages/frontpage.asp) (פשיטא).
- From the [About page](https://lib.cet.ac.il/pages/about.asp): “The virtual library project of Metah began in 2000. Metah is a non-profit institution and the library project is non-commercial; The library is open and accessible to anyone for free.”
- Some examples of articles available:
  - 55 Tarbitz (תרביץ) articles, see [list](https://lib.cet.ac.il/pages/sub.asp?source=139).

entries.name: Ad Henah
entries.summary: PDFs of Hebrew scholarly articles from an institute that studies the Torah works of Galician and Bukovina Jewry.
entries.annotation_md:
- Lots of PDFs of scholarly articles in Hebrew.
- From the [About page](http://jgbherzog.jgaliciabukovina.net/index.php/he/node/2): “A study and research institute that studies the Torah work of Galician and Bukovina Jewry, from the sixteenth century to the present time.”

entries.name: Ptil Tekhelet
entries.summary: Library of about 530 PDF scholarly articles in Hebrew on the topic of tekhelet.
entries.annotation_md: - Lots of PDFs of scholarly articles in Hebrew (shows 530 items). Focuses on the topic of tekhelet.

entries.name: Author academic websites
entries.summary: Scholars' personal academic websites, usually hosted by their university, often share their articles.
entries.annotation_md: Author academic websites, generally hosted on the website of the university that they’re affiliated with (e.g. [Yehuda Liebes](https://liebes.huji.ac.il/))

entries.name: Humanities Commons
entries.summary: Open repository of humanities papers; its “Hebrew Literature” tag holds a small number of papers.
entries.annotation_md: The tag “Hebrew Literature” has 16 papers.

entries.name: Ask the author
entries.summary: Writing to the author directly is often an effective way to get a copy of an article or dissertation.
entries.annotation_md: Ask the author - generally amenable to sending their own articles and dissertation.

entries.name: National Library of Israel - ordering scans
entries.summary: Paid service of the National Library of Israel for ordering scans and prints of items from its collections.
entries.annotation_md: National Library of Israel has a service for ordering scans from the library collections ([הזמנת סריקות והדפסות מאוספי הספרייה](https://www.nli.org.il/he/at-your-service/document-delivery-service/scans-within-library)). See also: [הזמנת צילומים מיוחדים](https://web.nli.org.il/sites/NLI/Hebrew/library/services/interlibrary%20loan/Pages/photos_loan.aspx).

entries.name: RAMBI
entries.summary: The National Library of Israel's index of articles in Jewish Studies and Israel studies, the largest database of its kind.
entries.annotation_md:
- My understanding is that “The Bibliography of The Hebrew Book” has been incorporated into “Merhav” (see above).
- [Wikipedia - Hebrew](https://he.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D7%A8%D7%9E%D7%91%22%D7%99): “An indexed and cataloged article index (or bibliography) of thousands of academic and other articles in a wide range of fields in the Jewish Studies, the study of the Land of Israel and the State of Israel, and is the largest and most comprehensive database of its kind in the world. The information contained in Rambi was collected from thousands of scientific journals, literary or documentary journals, collections and files of one-time articles on a specific topic, in Hebrew, English, French, German and other languages and in the Judaic languages: Yiddish, Arabic, Ladino and others; most of them found in the National Library of Israel. The criteria for inclusion in Rambi are that the publication be in an academic publication or another recognized and respected stage, or that it be useful for academic research purposes.”

entries.name: RAMBISH
entries.summary: An article index like RAMBI, but for articles in Orthodox (Torah) journals.
entries.annotation_md: Same concept as RAMBI, but for articles appearing in Orthodox journals.

entries.name: Cotar Project - Collection of Torah Articles
entries.summary: Database of Torah journals and periodicals, with a list of periodicals and a breakdown by topic.
entries.annotation_md: - A database of Torah journals/periodicals. Has a list of periodicals, and also breakdown by topic.
footnotes_md: 61. This resource was pointed out by the commenter “Sam” to the pt. 2 blogpost. Some functionality of “Cotar” doesn’t work on Chrome or other Chromium browsers; it requires Internet Explorer and a specific plug-in, which for technical reasons I was unable to test.
entries.status_note: Footnote 61: some functionality requires Internet Explorer and a specific plug-in.

entries.name: Indexes of dissertations / theses
entries.summary: Search pages and lists of Jewish Studies dissertations at the Hebrew University, Bar-Ilan University, and JTS.
entries.annotation_md:
- [Hebrew University](http://www.huji.ac.il/htbin/doctors/index.cgi?tofes) - search
- [Bar-Ilan University, Jewish Studies Department](https://www2.biu.ac.il/Academics/phd_heb/index-JSn.html) - list
- [Jewish Theological Seminary](https://digitalcollections.jtsa.edu/islandora/object/jts%3A617619)- search and list

entries.name: Google Scholar
entries.summary: Google's general search engine for scholarly literature.

entries.name: Tiresias: The Ancient Mediterranean Religions Source Database
entries.summary: Aggregates about 700 back-of-book subject and text indices on ancient Mediterranean religions, Rabbinics included; searchable by subject or source text.
entries.annotation_md: - “An aggregation of (currently about 700) back-of-book indices, both subject and text indices. It is by no means limited to Rabbinics, but includes them.”
footnotes_md: 62. Private communication from Dr. Moshe Blidstein. He wrote to me further: “you can read a short About section on the site, or a longer description here: [https://www.digitalhumanities.org/dhq/vol/17/1/000651/000651.html](https://www.digitalhumanities.org/dhq/vol/17/1/000651/000651.html). There are a number of options, we can look at a subject - e.g., [https://tiresias.haifa.ac.il/?subj=burial](https://tiresias.haifa.ac.il/?subj=burial). This will give all kinds of things, but certainly include also Rabbinics results (if you scroll down). The search can also be limited chronologically to the relevant centuries if more focus is needed. It is true that in such subjects the main perspective of the site is comparative. You can also look at subjects which are "Jewish", e.g., [https://tiresias.haifa.ac.il/?subj=synagogue](https://tiresias.haifa.ac.il/?subj=synagogue) will of course be more focused. The other way if through texts. the general list is here: [https://tiresias.haifa.ac.il/texts](https://tiresias.haifa.ac.il/texts) b. sanhedrin, for example: [https://tiresias.haifa.ac.il/?subj=ezezez:1778](https://tiresias.haifa.ac.il/?subj=ezezez:1778). If you click in to one of the pages (preferably one with alot of subjects) you get a list of intertexts, subjects, and of the books discussing this text.”

entries.name: Index of References Dealing with Talmudic Literature (Lieberman Index)
entries.summary: Subscription index that gives pinpointed citations from hundreds of scholarly works for specific passages of Talmudic literature.
entries.annotation_md:
Requires subscription.
- From the home page:
  - “The Index of References Dealing with Talmudic Literature, offering pinpointed citations from hundreds of classic and modern scholarly works directly related to the specific selected passage within Talmudic literature.”

entries.name: Oxford Bibliographies in Jewish Studies
entries.summary: Subscription database of annotated bibliographic articles across all fields and periods of Jewish Studies.
entries.annotation_md:
Requires subscription.
- From [Bar-Ilan University’s library guide](https://lib.biu.ac.il/en/node/1702): “Oxford Bibliographies in Jewish Studies is an interdisciplinary database encompassing history, religion, philosophy, literature, sociology and political science. Its chronological and geographical range stretches from the Bible to the present, including communities from the Americas to Western and Eastern Europe, North Africa and the Middle East, South and East Asia, and Africa. Oxford Bibliographies Jewish Studies offers selected articles that break down subject areas into their component parts and pithy annotations that summarize the main contribution of each citation. The database is one of the components of the Oxford Bibliography, a database that offers an authoritative guide to the current scholarship, containing original commentary and annotations.”

entries.name: Jewish Encyclopedia
entries.summary: The early-20th-century English Jewish Encyclopedia online; much of it has been absorbed into English Wikipedia.
entries.annotation_md:
In English.
- Large parts of it have been incorporated into the corresponding English Wikipedia entries.

entries.name: Wikipedia - Hebrew
entries.summary: Hebrew Wikipedia, a strong source on Jewish topics such as biographies, communities, and Jewish law.
entries.annotation_md:
- Great source for Jewish topics. I personally have found Wikipedia to be great sources for, among other topics:
  - Biographies of Jews
  - Jewish communities
  - Jewish Law (halacha)

entries.name: Hamichlol
entries.summary: Haredi wiki encyclopedia built mostly on Hebrew Wikipedia; its original entries are strong on Jewish topics, especially rabbis' biographies.
entries.annotation_md:
- Wikipedia - Hebrew: “Hamichlol is a wiki-based Haredi encyclopedia. As of 2023, most of the entries in the collection are exact copies of Hebrew Wikipedia entries or filtered versions of them for ultra-Orthodox. Next to them, it has entries that were originally written for Hamichlol. The website was launched in 2015.”
- The entries original to Hamichlol are especially strong for Jewish topics, especially biographies of rabbis.

entries.name: Encyclopedia Talmudit - Micropedia
entries.summary: Concise Micropedia and new entries of the Talmudic Encyclopedia, hosted on Wikishiva, in rabbinic and modern Hebrew.
entries.annotation_md:
In rabbinic/modern Hebrew, on Talmudic topics.
- From the webpage: “From Micropedia to Encyclopedia: Wikishiva (ויקישיבה) continues its collaboration with the Talmudic Encyclopedia project and now becomes the home of the new Talmudic Encyclopedia entries. Now, beyond the Talmudic Micropedia project, the entries of the Encyclopedia itself will be published here. It is important to note that entries published here are not currently published as books. To date, 251 entries have been written in the Talmudic Encyclopedia project. The Talmudic Encyclopedia: The new Talmudic Encyclopedia entries are already on Wikishiva! You can browse all the entries on the site or search using the search box, select the first letter, or select from the new entries on the site. The Talmudic Micropedia: The Talmudic Micropedia is a concise and up-to-date treasure trove of the entries of the Talmudic Encyclopedia, in a flowing and clear style.”

entries.name: Encyclopedia Judaica, 2nd edition
entries.summary: The second edition of Encyclopaedia Judaica on Gale (subscription, often via libraries); entries also seem to appear on encyclopedia.com.
entries.annotation_md:
In English.
- Second edition published by Gale and available on their website. Requires subscription, many libraries give access through OpenAthens, see for example [Bar-Ilan University’s page](https://lib.biu.ac.il/en/node/264).
- The entries (all? some?) of Encyclopedia Judaica, 2nd edition, appear to have been incorporated into encyclopedia.com, and fully hyperlinked to other EJ entries. The entries seem to be able to be found only via search, there’s no way to browse list of entries. See [google search "Encyclopaedia Judaica site:https://www.encyclopedia.com/"](https://www.google.com/search?q=Encyclopaedia+Judaica+site%3Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.encyclopedia.com%2F&lr=&safe=images&as_qdr=all&sxsrf=AOaemvKXF14_YwN1km1VZc1A5Ydsgo3PZg%3A1643176582404&ei=huLwYeb2F_2p9u8PwNiUwAk&ved=0ahUKEwjm0fzj3c71AhX9lP0HHUAsBZgQ4dUDCA4&uact=5&oq=Encyclopaedia+Judaica+site%3Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.encyclopedia.com%2F&gs_lcp=Cgdnd3Mtd2l6EAM6BwgAEEcQsANKBAhBGABKBAhGGABQ7ANYtDBg-zNoAXACeACAAWuIAdYBkgEDMC4ymAEAoAECoAEByAEDwAEB&sclient=gws-wiz).
- Bar-Ilan University overview: “Provides an overview of Jewish life and knowledge from the Second Temple period to the contemporary State of Israel, from Rabbinic to modern Yiddish literature, from Kabbalah to "Americana" and from Zionism to the contribution of Jews to world cultures.”

entries.name: Encyclopedias published by Brill
entries.summary: Four Brill online reference works: Encyclopaedia of Judaism, Jews in the Islamic World, Jewish History and Culture, and Hebrew Language and Linguistics.
entries.annotation_md:
In English:
- [Encyclopaedia of Judaism Online](https://brill.com/view/db/ejo).
  - From the webpage: “The prize-winning Encyclopaedia of Judaism is now available online. More than 200 entries comprising more than 1,000,000 words. This unique reference tool offers an authoritative, comprehensive, and systematic presentation of the current state of scholarship on fundamental issues of Judaism, both past and present. Comprehensive and up-to-date, it reflects the highest standards in scholarship. Covering a tradition of nearly four thousand years, some of the most distinguished scholars in the field describe the way of life, history, art, theology, philosophy, and the practices and beliefs of the Jewish people.”
- [Encyclopedia of Jews in the Islamic World Online.](https://brill.com/view/db/ejio)
  - From the webpage: “[T]he first cohesive and discreet reference work which covers the Jews of Muslim lands particularly in the late medieval, early modern and modern periods. The expanded online version, EJIW Online (started in 2010), is updated twice annually with newly commissioned articles, illustrations, multimedia, and primary source material. Interdisciplinary articles cover a wide range of topics from history, law, music, visual arts, social sciences, philosophy, anthropology and demography.”
- [Encyclopedia of Jewish History and Culture Online](https://brill.com/view/db/ejhc).
  - From the webpage: “From Europe to America to the Middle East, North Africa and other non-European Jewish settlement areas the Encyclopedia of Jewish History and Culture covers the recent history of the Jews from 1750 until the 1950s. Translated from German into English, approximately 800 keywords present the current state of international research and depict a complex portrait of Jewish life - illustrated by many maps and images. About 40 key articles convey central themes on topics like autonomy, exile, emancipation, literature, liturgy, music or the science of Judaism.”
- [Encyclopedia of Hebrew Language and Linguistics Online](https://brill.com/view/db/ehhl).
  - From the webpage: “[A] systematic and comprehensive treatment of all aspects of the history and study of the Hebrew language from its earliest attested form to the present day. The encyclopedia contains overview articles that provide a readable synopsis of current knowledge of the major periods and varieties of the Hebrew language as well as thematically-organized entries which provide further information on individual topics. With over 950 entries and approximately 400 contributing scholars, the Encyclopedia of Hebrew Language and Linguistics is the authoritative reference work for students and researchers in the fields of Hebrew linguistics, general linguistics, Biblical studies, Hebrew and Jewish literature, and related fields.”

entries.name: Wiktionary - Hebrew
entries.summary: Hebrew Wiktionary, with generally good entries that cite many primary and secondary sources.
entries.annotation_md: (H). Generally very good entries, with ample primary and secondary sources.

entries.name: Jastrow’s A Dictionary of the Targumim, the Talmud Babli and Yerushalmi, and the Midrashic Literature
entries.summary: Jastrow's English dictionary of Talmudic and Midrashic Hebrew and Aramaic, online at Sefaria, Wikisource, and Tyndale House.
entries.annotation_md:
In English:
- Sefaria: [here](https://www.sefaria.org/Jastrow). Transcribed and searchable, with hyperlinked Table of Contents.
- Wiktionary: [here](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/A_Dictionary_of_the_Targumim,_the_Talmud_Babli_and_Yerushalmi,_and_the_Midrashic_Literature). Transcribed, with hyperlinked Table of Contents.
- Tyndale House: [here](http://www.tyndalearchive.com/TABS/Jastrow//). Scanned, with hyperlinked Table of Contents.

entries.name: Ben-Yehuda Dictionary
entries.name_he: מילון בן-יהודה - מילון העברית הישנה והחדשה
entries.summary: Eliezer Ben-Yehuda's dictionary of old and new Hebrew, transcribed with a hyperlinked table of contents.
entries.annotation_md: Transcribed, with hyperlinked Table of Contents.

entries.name: R’ Natan of Rome, Sefer HeArukh, ed. Lublin 1883
entries.summary: The medieval Talmudic lexicon HeArukh with Musafia's Musaf HeArukh on Sefaria, plus Isaiah Berlin's glosses on it.
entries.annotation_md: [R’ Natan of Rome, Sefer HeArukh, ed. Lublin 1883](https://www.sefaria.org/Sefer_HeArukh), on [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org/Sefer_HeArukh). Includes R’ Benjamin Mousafia’s Musaf Aruch. Also at Sefaria: [R’ Isaiah Berlin’s Hafla'ah ShebaArakhin on Sefer HeArukh](https://www.sefaria.org/Hafla'ah_ShebaArakhin_on_Sefer_HeArukh).

entries.name: Academy of Hebrew language’s online dictionary
entries.summary: The Hebrew Language Academy's Modern Hebrew online dictionary, based on Milon HaHoveh, without etymologies or sources.
entries.annotation_md: In Modern Hebrew. Based on Milon HaHoveh (מילון ההווה). Does not include etymologies or sources.

entries.name: Zohar Dictionary by Daniel Matt
entries.summary: Daniel Matt's dictionary of Zohar vocabulary.

entries.name_he: גרשם שלום, כרטסת שלום, לקסיקון לספר הזוהר
entries.summary: Scans of Gershom Scholem's index cards for his Zohar lexicon, at the National Library of Israel.
